title: Other Worlds
caption: ALMA antennas under a sky with Alpha Centauri, Antares and Saturn, Chajnantor plateau
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Two bright stars sit directly above the central antenna in this group of dishes on the Chajnantor plateau in Chile, part of the 66 that make up ALMA, photographed by Y. Beletsky. According to the source, the brighter of the two is Alpha Centauri, a triple star system. At the top of the frame, two bright reddish objects lie just outside the main band of the Milky Way. The left one is Antares, a red giant star in Scorpius. The right one is Saturn, the ringed planet.

One of the most exciting findings of modern astronomy is that the Universe is full of exoplanets, worlds beyond our Solar System. Growing evidence suggests most stars have planets. ESO telescopes and other facilities discovered one, Proxima b, orbiting within the habitable zone of Proxima Centauri, one of Alpha Centauri's three stars. Since no star system lies closer to Earth than Alpha Centauri, Proxima b is the nearest exoplanet ever found.

understand.summary: This is a night landscape photograph by Y. Beletsky. The source gives no camera or color details.
understand.eye: The planet Proxima b cannot be seen in this photograph or by eye, and the photograph gathers far more light than the eye.
